source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.6
text: Cambodia officially recommends a set of rice varieties bred by CARDI, grouped into three duration/season classes with their own approximate crop calendars: (1) Early/short-duration wet-season varieties (ស្រូវស្រាល) — e.g. IR66 (អ៊ីអឹ៦៦), Chulsar (ជលសារ), and Sen Pidor (សែនពីដោរ) — these can be sown roughly around January and again around June, allowing more than one planting window per year. (2) Medium-duration varieties (ស្រូវកណ្តាល) — e.g. Phka Rumduol (ផ្កាវជូល), Phka Rumdeng (ផ្កាវជេង), Phka Malis (ផ្កាវម្លៀត), and Phka Chan Sen Sor (ផ្កាច័ន្ទសែនសរ) — typically sown around June. (3) Long-duration/photoperiod-sensitive wet-season varieties (ស្រូវធន់) — e.g. Riang Chey (រាំងជ័យ), Khsach 84 (ខសាច់៨៤), and Khsach 86 (ខសាច់៨៦). In total there are 10 CARDI-bred seed varieties recommended and distributed nationally. Within the APPP project's operating area (Battambang province), Phka Rumduol (ផ្កាវជូល) is reported to be planted on nearly 100% of the seed-production area.
